title: SectionedTree renders two expand-all controls with the same label and configures only one
foundBy: session agent, building patterns/NavSidebar.md, at the owner's request to record what was hard

evidence.verified: `src/components/SectionedTree.expandAll.test.tsx` counts each kind of control through its own hook across all four values of the prop: `true` renders one sections control and two per-section ones, `false` renders none, `"sections"` and `"trees"` render one kind each. A fifth test holds the two accessible names apart. Two reverts fail the tests that cover them: rendering the sections control unconditionally fails the `false` and `"trees"` cases, and giving both controls the same label again fails the naming test. Restores were byte-identical. The nav sidebar capture loses the control it could not remove, at 8053 differing pixels in the light theme, and four comparison runs after the re-record passed. `npm run ci` exits 0 at 7a26aea.

details:
`SectionedTree` renders a control above the sections reading `Collapse all`, and gives each section's `Tree` another that reads `Collapse all` too. `expandAllControl` turns off the second kind and not the first, and neither the prop's name nor `components/SectionedTree.md` says so.

Two consequences, both met while building the nav sidebar pattern. A reader looking at the rendered page cannot tell which control `expandAllControl` governs. And a test asserting `queryAllByRole("button", { name: /expand all/i })` is empty passes whether the prop works or not, because the surviving control reads `Collapse all` while the sections are open. That assertion was written in this session and had to be replaced with a count.

The sections control also has no prop of its own, so a sidebar that does not want it cannot remove it.

The smallest honest fix is to name them differently in the DOM, through distinct accessible names or a `data-part`, and to say in the specification which one `expandAllControl` reaches. Giving the sections control its own prop is the larger version.

notes.text:
The larger fix was taken, at the owner's decision, and without keeping `false` backward compatible. `expandAllControl` reaches both kinds of control now, so `false` removes both where it used to leave the sections one standing.

Two tests in the repository had encoded the defect. One in `SectionedTree.chrome.test.tsx` asserted only that the count fell when the prop was set, which passed while one control ignored it. One in `patterns.wiring.test.tsx` asserted the nav sidebar kept exactly one control, which was the one it could not remove. Both now count each kind through its own hook.

A second defect came out of the work and is filed as CUI-063. The per-section control sits inside the toolbar that `filterable` gates, so turning off a filter box takes an unrelated control with it.
